title: Quantum-Safe Code Auditing: LLM-Assisted Static Analysis and Quantum-Aware Risk Scoring for Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration
abs: The impending arrival of cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQCs) threatens the security foundations of modern software: Shor's algorithm breaks RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, and Diffie-Hellman, while Grover's algorithm reduces the effective security of symmetric and hash-based schemes. Despite NIST standardising post-quantum cryptography (PQC) in 2024 (FIPS 203 ML-KEM, FIPS 204 ML-DSA, FIPS 205 SLH-DSA), most codebases lack automated tooling to inventory classical cryptographic usage and prioritise migration based on quantum risk. We present Quantum-Safe Code Auditor, a quantum-aware static analysis framework that combines (i) regex-based detection of 15 classes of quantum-vulnerable primitives, (ii) LLM-assisted contextual enrichment to classify usage and severity, and (iii) risk scoring via a Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) model implemented in Qiskit 2.x, incorporating qubit-cost estimates to prioritise findings. We evaluate the system across five open-source libraries -- python-rsa, python-ecdsa, python-jose, node-jsonwebtoken, and Bouncy Castle Java -- covering 5,775 findings. On a stratified sample of 602 labelled instances, we achieve 71.98% precision, 100% recall, and an F1 score of 83.71%. All code, data, and reproduction scripts are released as open-source.

title: Efficient DPF-based Error-Detecting Information-Theoretic Private Information Retrieval Over Rings
abs: Authenticated private information retrieval (APIR) is the state-of-the-art error-detecting private information retrieval (ED-PIR), using Distributed Point Functions (DPFs) for subpolynomial complexity and privacy. However, its finite field structure restricts it to prime-order DPFs, leading to prohibitively large key sizes under information-theoretic settings, while its dual-DPF-key design introduces unnecessary communication overhead, limiting its practicality for large-scale deployments. This paper proposes a novel ring-based information-theoretic ED-PIR (itED-PIR) scheme that overcomes these limitations by leveraging prime-power-order information-theoretic DPFs (itDPFs). Built over a prime-power ring, the proposed scheme breaks APIR's field-induced constraint to enable more efficient DPF utilization, significantly reducing key size growth and rendering the scheme feasible for high-security scenarios. Additionally, a single-itDPF-key design halves query-side communication overhead by eliminating APIR's redundant dual-key setup, without compromising privacy or verifiability. Beyond immediate efficiency gains, this work establishes a lightweight, flexible framework for constructing DPF-based malicious-resilient private information retrieval, opening new avenues for privacy-preserving data retrieval in distributed storage systems and post-quantum privacy protocols.

title: Post-Quantum Cryptographic Algorithms Performance Evaluation of Secure Networked Systems
journal: 2026 Fourth International Conference on Augmented Intelligence and Sustainable Systems (ICAISS)
abs: It is also worth noting that the implementation of quantum computing has been a big threat to the classical cryptographic algorithms that are popular in secure networked systems. PostQuantum Cryptography (PQC) has come to play as one of the viable answers to this issue because it has the capacity to resist quantum-enabled attacks. In this paper, the author offers a detailed performance analysis of post-quantum cryptographic algorithms, lattice-based encryption which is based on the Learning with Errors (LWE) principle, and hashbased digital signatures which is based on SPHINCS+. An experimental environment was created that is controlled by using specific performance measures, such as time of key generation, the latency of encryption and decryption, amount of memory, and the size of keys and ciphertext. To determine the suitability of PQC in guaranteeing confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity over insecure channels, secure network communication was emulated. Through experimental findings, it has been shown that the lattice-based generation of keys has greater overhead in terms of computation and memory, but the encryption, decryption and signature processes have feasible limits. The results validate the practicability of the post-quantum cryptography mechanisms implementation in the practical secure network systems and the trade-off between the increased quantum resistance and the resource consumption.

title: Dependency-Aware Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration Planning: Graph-Based Optimization for Enterprise Infrastructure
abs: The transition to post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) algorithms requires enterprises to migrate thousands of cryptographic assets from vulnerable algorithms (RSA, ECDSA, DH, DSA) to NIST-standardized replacements (ML-KEM, ML-DSA), but uncoordinated migration introduces interoperability failures when migrated assets cannot communicate with unmigrated dependents. This paper presents an automated migration planning platform that builds a cryptographic dependency graph, computes quantum risk scores with graph centrality, and generates an optimized migration plan using reversed topological ordering with risk-weighted prioritization. A factorial experiment (3 scales × 3 strategies × 10 seeds = 90 runs) on simulated enterprises with 100 to 10,000 assets shows that the dependency-aware strategy reduces cumulative quantum risk exposure 26% faster than random ordering (p < 0.001), eliminates 88.6% of interoperability failures (p = 0.028), and scales from 14% AUC improvement at 100 nodes to 41% at 10,000 nodes. The core mechanism is processing dependency graph leaves first, ensuring that when a server transitions to PQC, its dependent applications already speak the new protocol.

title: Defensive Intelligent Traffic Management using Secure AI Intersection Control, Resilient Sensor Fusion, and Crisis-Aware Autonomous Routing
abs: This paper introducesDefensive Intelligent Traffic Management (DITM), a defense-grade architectural paradigm designed to ensure secure AI intersection control, resilient multisensor fusion, post-quantum identity assurance for all infrastructure nodes, and crisis-aware autonomous routing capable of preserving emergency mobility and critical logistics under sustained cyber-physical stress. The framework integrates tamper-evident control flows, neurosymbolic law-compliance gates, federated edge learning, and sovereign supervisory authority to guarantee that autonomous transport functions remain lawful, auditable, and aligned with public-safety doctrine. A metropolitan-scale digital-twin simulation encompassing 320 intersections demonstrates improvements in emergency-vehicle travel time, spoofing resistance, congestion-collapse prevention, and continuity of routing decisions under adversarial conditions. The results establish a deployable blueprint for national-scale, security-centric, and ethically aligned autonomous traffic governance. DITM reorients intelligent mobility from algorithmic efficiency toward secure, mission-critical resilience, forming the foundation for sovereign AI-driven transport infrastructure.

title: Post-Quantum Cryptographic Framework for Infrastructure Protection
abs: Quantum computing is rapidly approaching a stage where classical cryptographic systems, particularly RSA, ECC, and Diffie─Hellman, will no longer provide adequate security for critical infrastructure. The emergence of Shor's and Grover's algorithms introduces unprecedented vulnerability to national cyber-defense ecosystems, underpinning power grids, transportation, military communications, and banking systems. This paper presents a unified post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) security framework integrating lattice-based primitives, hybrid key-exchange mechanisms, and secure orchestration for resource-constrained operational-technology environments. The proposed architecture leverages NIST-recommended schemes, including CRYSTALS-Kyber, CRYSTALS-Dilithium, and SPHINCS+, to ensure long-term confidentiality, integrity, and interoperability across legacy and modern control environments. A defense-in-depth trust-fabric is introduced to protect critical data flows across edge controllers, automation PLCs, substations, cloud-SCADA gateways, and defense communication systems. Performance evaluation demonstrates a 39.4% reduction in key-exchange latency, 46% faster authentication cycles, and zero-downtime cryptographic transition capability. Our findings position this framework as a practical migration blueprint supporting national PQC readiness and cyber-resilience mandates.

title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Machine Learning for Cybersecurity Threat Detection and Intrusion Prediction: a Systematic Review
journal: 2026 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications Theme: Healthcare and Internet of Things (AIMLA)
abs: The paper presents a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review of hybrid quantum-classical machine learning (HQCML) for cybersecurity intrusion detection, with emphasis on the Store Now, Decrypt Later (SNDL) threat. Searching five databases, 87 primary studies (2018-2024) were identified; 72 passed a Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) quality threshold$(\geq 6 / 10)$, with sensitivity analysis at$\geq 7 / 10$yielding 58 studies and consistent results ($\kappa=0.83$). Amplitude-encoded variational quantum circuit (VQC) classifiers match deep learning accuracy with significantly fewer trainable parameters. Three key barriers emerge: 80.6 % of studies rely solely on simulation, inference latency is incompatible with line-rate monitoring, and barren plateau instability limits training at scale. A sevenitem research agenda addresses hardware validation, dataset development, and SNDL-specific benchmarking.

title: Zero-Trust Post-Quantum Cryptographic Framework for Securing SCADA Communication
journal: 2026 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications Theme: Healthcare and Internet of Things (AIMLA)
abs: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems represent the cyber-physical infrastructure core of critical infrastructure, where any security violation can cause severe operational and physical repercussions. The integration of operational technology with Information Technology networks has introduced new vulnerabilities to cyber attacks, while the emergence of quantum computing poses a basic threat to classical cryptographic approaches currently in use within industrial control systems. This paper presents a novel Zero-Trust Post-Quantum Cryptographic (ZT-PQC) solution specifically tailored for resource-constrained SCADA systems. The solution combines lightweight symmetric encryption for field devices, hybrid and pure post-quantum cryptography for higher layers, and continuous Zero-Trust policy enforcement throughout the communication process. A layer-aware cryptographic offloading approach is utilized to strike a balance between quantum resilience and real-time operational requirements. The feasibility of the proposed solution is assessed using a validated synthetic SCADA dataset simulating practical communication patterns, attack models, and system constraints. Experimental results show that the solution provides quantum-resistant security with acceptable latency, minimal communication overhead, and compatibility with existing SCADA systems, thus being amenable to incremental deployment in critical infrastructure systems.

title: Analysis of 64-Bit Booth-MAC Based Processing Element for NTT Acceleration
journal: 2026 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications Theme: Healthcare and Internet of Things (AIMLA)
abs: Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) is an important computational kernel applied in polynomial multiplication for post-quantum cryptography and other high-security applications. High-precision arithmetic and fast multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations are necessary for efficient hardware realization of NTT. Unfortunately, most existing hardware implementations of NTT are based on low bit-width arithmetic and traditional multipliers, which are performance and scalability bottlenecks for NTT acceleration. This paper introduces the design and RTL implementation of a 64bit Booth-MAC-based processing element (PE) tailored for NTT acceleration. The proposed design combines a Radix-4 Booth multiplier, a 64-bit adder, and an accumulator register to support efficient signed multiply-accumulate operations. Radix-4 Booth encoding minimizes partial products, thus enhancing computational efficiency and hardware complexity. The whole design is developed at the front-end VLSI level using Verilog HDL and validated by simulation using various signed test vectors. Simulation results confirm the correctness of the proposed processing element for positive, negative, and zero operands. The modular and scalable design can be applied as a building block for systolic array-based NTT accelerators. The proposed solution fills the existing gap between algorithm-level NTT architectures and RTL-level hardware realization for high-precision cryptographic systems.

title: A Secure Multi-Modal AI-Driven Blockchain Voting Framework with Post-Quantum Encryption and Deepfake-Resilient Authentication
journal: 2026 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications Theme: Healthcare and Internet of Things (AIMLA)
abs: The growing digitalization of the electoral system has created a serious question of security, privacy, and integrity. To address them, the following paper suggests a proposal of a Secure Multi-Modal AI-Driven Blockchain Voting Framework, which will employ artificial intelligence, block chain technology, Internet of Things (IOT), and post-quantum cryptography to develop a stable and resistant to future digital voting system. The suggested model involves the application of multi-modal biometric authentication, including the use of deep learning-based face recognition and the one-time password authentication to ensure high and deep fake-impregnable voter authentication and check against the cases of illegal and repeated voting. Voting machines that are IOT ready allow real-time voting which is secured and the votes are encrypted using post-quantum cryptographic algorithms before being stored in an indestructible block chain registry to ensure confidentiality, integrity and transparency. The experimental results indicate that the offered system allows attaining high levels of authentication between 96.85 % and 98.72 %, which is significantly higher than the current machine learning-based methods, and demonstrates the high level of protection against fraud and impersonation attacks. The results indicate that the suggested framework can be scaled, is tamper-proof, privacy secure, and has long-term durability against emerging cyber threats therefore enhancing voter trust and guaranteeing reliable digital governance.

title: Post-Quantum Entropy as a Service for Embedded Systems
abs: Embedded cryptography stands or falls on entropy quality, yet small devices have few trustworthy sources and little tolerance for heavyweight protocols. We build a Quantum Entropy as a Service (QEaaS) system that moves QRNG-derived entropy from a Quantis device to ESP32-class clients over post-quantum-secured channels. On the server side, the design exposes two paths: direct quantum entropy through a custom OpenSSL provider and mixed entropy through the Linux system pool. On the client side, we extend libcoap's Zephyr support, integrate wolfSSL-based DTLS 1.3 into the CoAP stack, and add a BLAKE2s entropy pool that preserves the standard Zephyr extraction interface while introducing an injection API for server-provided entropy. Benchmarks on ESP32 hardware, targeting 100 iterations per configuration, show that ML-KEM-512 completes a DTLS 1.3 handshake in 313 ms on average without certificate verification, 35% faster than ECDHE P-256. Pairing ML-KEM-512 with ML-DSA-44 lowers the mean to 225 ms. Certificate verification adds roughly 194 ms for ECDSA but only 17 ms for ML-DSA-44, so the fully post-quantum configuration remains 63% faster than classical ECDHE P-256 with ECDSA even under full verification. Local BLAKE2s pool operations stay below 0.1 ms combined. On this platform, post-quantum key exchange and authentication are not only feasible; they are faster than the classical baseline.

title: PhysioKey: Edge-AI-Driven Physiological Key Agreement for Secure Body Area Networks
abs: Body area networks (BANs) require secure intra-body communication, yet sensor nodes are too resource-constrained for conventional public-key cryptography, and pre-shared key schemes conflict with plug-and-play clinical workflows. This paper introduces PhysioKey, a TinyML-based key agreement framework that derives symmetric session keys from physiological signals without pre-shared secrets or trusted third parties. A lightweight 1D-CNN (6320 parameters, INT8-quantized, 31.2 KB flash) extracts embeddings from ECG and PPG windows on ARM Cortex-M4 class devices, which are reconciled through fuzzy commitment with BCH error-correcting codes. Patient-level 5-fold cross-validation on PTB-XL (500 patients, dual-ECG) achieves EER of 7.8%±0.8% with ROC AUC 0.978±0.004; on BIDMC (53 patients, ECG + PPG), a dual-encoder architecture reduces cross-modal EER to 30.6%±1.2%. Since standalone PhysioKey yields only 7─24 effective key bits, the recommended deployment mode is a hybrid PhysioKey + ECDH protocol providing 128-bit security while PhysioKey adds physical on-body authentication; standalone operation suits energy-constrained scenarios with its 27× advantage over ECDH. HKDF-SHA-256 post-processing yields session keys passing all six NIST SP 800-22 tests (≥96% at the 1024-bit level).

title: SSDBFAN: Scalable and Secure Cluster-Based Data Aggregation with Blockchain for Flying Ad Hoc Networks
abs: Mobile Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) forming Flying Ad Hoc Networks (FANETs) offer promising applications, but dynamic network structures, limited resources, and potential single points of failure create security challenges. While cluster-based data aggregation, where data is collected and combined at Cluster Heads (CHs) before transmission, improves efficiency, traditional techniques can compromise data privacy. This paper introduces SSDBFAN, a scalable and secure cluster-based data aggregation framework for Flying Ad Hoc Networks (FANETs). The proposed approach integrates the Frilled Lizard Optimization Algorithm (FLOA) for efficient cluster head selection with blockchain technology and post-quantum cryptographic techniques, including lattice-based homomorphic encryption and the Chinese Remainder Theorem, to ensure privacy-preserving data aggregation. Additionally, a hybrid online/offline signature mechanism is employed to achieve secure and efficient authentication with reduced computational overhead. The performance of the proposed framework is evaluated using NS-3 simulations under varying network sizes. Experimental results demonstrate that SSDBFAN significantly improves communication efficiency, reduces computational cost, and enhances network stability compared to existing schemes. Furthermore, scalability analysis with up to 500 UAV nodes confirms that the proposed framework effectively controls blockchain overhead, including bandwidth consumption, consensus latency, and storage requirements. Comparative evaluation with existing optimization algorithms shows that FLOA achieves superior performance in terms of cluster stability, delay, and throughput. These results validate the effectiveness of SSDBFAN as a scalable and security-aware solution for large-scale FANET environments.

title: QADR: quantum-assisted protocol for anonymous data reporting
abs: The security of future large-scale IoT networks is critically threatened by the "Harvest Now, Decrypt Later" (HNDL) attack paradigm. Securing the massive, long-lived data streams from these systems requires protocols that are both quantum-resistant and highly scalable. Existing solutions are insufficient: Post-quantum classical protocols rely on computational assumptions that may not hold for decades, while purely quantum protocols are too resource-intensive for the sheer scale of IoT. This paper introduces the Quantum Anonymous Data Reporting (QADR) protocol, a hybrid framework that provides a theoretical benchmark and high-performance architecture for this challenge, designed for future fully connected quantum networks. The protocol achieves scalable, quantum-resistant anonymity through a hybrid security model; it leverages information-theoretically secure keys from quantum key distribution (QKD) to seed a quantum-secure pseudorandom function (QS-PRF), grounding its long-term data protection in well-established computational hardness assumptions. We also propose and analyze an automated slot reservation mechanism by making a deliberate trade-off: achieving high performance by accepting a quantifiable information leak during the anonymous slot reservation phase while maintaining strong unlinkability for the final data submission. Our security analysis formally quantifies the anonymity reduction caused by the leak and discusses pathways to fully mitigate it at a significant performance cost. We prove the protocol's critical advantage as a performance benchmark: Its primary communication cost scales as O(n2), a dramatic improvement over quantum-native alternatives (O(n4)), establishing a high-performance goal for future quantum-secured anonymity systems.

title: Confidential integrity verification via quantum teleportation
abs: Standard post-quantum cryptography signatures can verify authenticity but inevitably compromise confidentiality by exposing message digests to the public channel—a critical vulnerability for low-entropy or high-security messages. To overcome this, we propose a Confidential Integrity Verification framework that functionally operates as a secure two-party equality test (Quantum Private Comparison). This framework verifies the integrity of shared messages without revealing their digests. Unlike classical and quantum authenticated encryption schemes, our protocol requires no pre-shared symmetric keys; it leverages post-quantum cryptography solely for authenticating the initial entanglement purification. The message equality comparison itself achieves information-theoretic confidentiality via quantum state teleportation. We demonstrate that even under realistic noisy channels, the authentication error probability can be suppressed below 10<SUP>−9</SUP> with only 194 entangled pairs. This resource efficiency, combined with intrinsic immunity to 'harvest now, decrypt later' attacks on the digest, provides an end-to-end, quantum-resistant solution ideal for verifying privacy-sensitive information in quantum networks, such as data post-processing in quantum key distribution.

title: Quantum cryptanalysis of ultralightweight mutual authentication protocols: A Grover's search model
abs: Quantum computing developments hold the promise of transforming the IT security landscape. Advances in quantum processors have introduced new theoretical threats to traditional cryptographic primitives through algorithms such as Grover's search and Shor's factorization, which can be used to cryptanalyze symmetric and asymmetric ciphers, respectively; however, the practical realization of these attacks depends critically on the availability of Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computers (CRQCs). While current quantum hardware is still a considerable distance from achieving this threshold, the steady progress in technology suggests that the realization of CRQCs depends fundamentally on ongoing advances in scaling and engineering. In response to this emerging long-term threat, NIST has revised traditional encryption standards by introducing post-quantum cipher suites. While post-quantum cryptography research has primarily focused on conventional asymmetric cryptosystems, symmetric ultralightweight ciphers—commonly employed in resource-constrained environments such as RFID systems—remain an underexplored target of quantum cryptanalysis. This work takes an initial step toward addressing this gap by demonstrating full disclosure attacks on three ultralightweight mutual authentication protocols: the Ultra-Lightweight RFID Authentication and Renewal Protocol (ULRARP+), the Lightweight RFID Authentication Protocol (LRAP), and the Ultra-Lightweight RFID Authentication Protocol (URAP). Based on these findings, the paper proposes a set of design principles to guide the development of quantum-resilient minimalist ciphers for the post-quantum era.

title: Neural-LWE: a biometric-anchored authenticated key agreement for post-quantum brain─computer interfaces
abs: The proliferation of Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs) and wireless Electroencephalography (EEG) devices necessitates security protocols that are simultaneously quantum-resistant and intrinsically linked to users' biological identity. While standard post-quantum cryptography like ML-KEM provides foundational security, it fails to address critical neurotechnology requirements: integrated biometric authentication, efficient long-term session management, and resilience to signal noise. This paper presents Neural-LWE (NLWE), a novel biometric-anchored authenticated key agreement protocol for quantum-secure Brain-Computer Interfaces. We introduce five fundamental innovations: (1) integration of Kalman-filtered EEG features with ML-KEM encapsulation for biometric two-factor authentication; (2) Zero-Communication-Round Rekeying (ZCRR) enabling 250 more efficient forward secrecy updates; (3) entropy-adaptive security dynamically scaling lattice parameters based on real-time EEG quality; (4) ternary-entropy masking for side-channel resistance; and (5) manifold-based anomaly detection against presentation attacks. NLWE establishes IND-CCA2 security under the Module-LWE (MLWE) assumption while addressing unique BCI constraints through formal cryptographic-biometric binding. Implementation results using physiologically plausible synthetic data confirm that ZCRR achieves 0.45J rekeying energy with sub-millisecond latency. While experimental validation is performed in a controlled environment, the results indicate NLWE is a promising proof-of-concept for continuous neural applications requiring persistent quantum security.

title: Enhancing IoT security through cloud-assisted post-quantum authentication: a case study with UOV signatures
abs: The UOV signature scheme is a promising quantum-resistant candidate in NIST PQC, offering shorter signatures and efficiency, but requires solving a system of linear equations, which presents a challenge while performing in resource-constrained IoT devices. This paper introduces the first-ever idea of securely delegating computationally intensive task in UOV signature generation to third-party (cloud) servers, assisting the implementation of post-quantum cryptographic schemes in resource-constrained devices. The proposed "cloud-assisted" UOV signature scheme uses an honest-but-curious cloud framework to facilitate efficient signature generation without compromising security. In addition, this protocol provides a provably secure framework for the privacy of the communicated data (both input and output), for securely generating a UOV signature. The efficacy of the proposed protocol is demonstrated via experimental evaluation and simulations implemented on a Raspberry Pi 5, providing evidence of a reduction in the computational burden and energy consumption in UOV signature generation using our proposed protocol.

title: Satellite-based quantum key distribution in the Arctic: a case study of Finnish Lapland
abs: The advent of quantum computing necessitates the transition from conventional encryption systems to quantum-resistant alternatives. Quantum key distribution (QKD) represents one such approach. Nevertheless, fibre-based QKD is constrained by severe limitations in transmission distance. A promising solution is satellite-based QKD, wherein a satellite establishes secure communication with a ground station. However, daylight presents a considerable challenge for QKD devices, which are highly sensitive to ambient light. Implementing satellite-based QKD in Arctic regions is particularly compelling due to their distinctive annual cycle and prolonged periods of darkness; yet, this possibility has received limited attention in the existing literature. This study assessed the feasibility of satellite-based QKD in regions above the Arctic Circle by simulating a satellite QKD link to three ground stations located in Finnish Lapland: Rovaniemi, Sodankylä, and Utsjoki. The simulation tool comprised MATLAB code for modelling the quantum link, satellite orbital data generated using the Python Skyfield library, and local weather data collected for the year 2024, including cloud cover, rain, snow, ice crystals, and fog. Our findings suggest that while the polar night provides favourable conditions for wintertime quantum communication, continuous daylight during summer and high cloud-cover probabilities may lead to extended service interruptions, severely limiting the achievable secret key material. Optimizing satellite overpass timing substantially reduces outage periods caused by background light; however, this optimization becomes ineffective during summer months due to the persistently high ambient light levels. These constraints underscore the need for robust key-storage mechanisms and careful evaluation of potential use cases. It is recommended that advanced filtering techniques be investigated as a potential means to mitigate summer outage periods caused by excessive ambient light.

title: Enhanced cloud security using post-quantum encryption techniques
journal: American Institute of Physics Conference Series
abs: Cloud Computing is widely used by various organizations wherein the user pays based on usage and flexing scaling of computing resources according to dynamic requirements. As this service can be accessed over the Internet, and plenty of users are accessing it; it might pose a threat to the data. A strong encryption technique is required to avoid various types of attacks. This paper mainly focuses on the designing of a post quantum cryptography technique based on encryption for Cloud Services. our study includes the theoretical analysis of how various orders of polynomials can affect the cryptographic security of IPCC7, and, once, its empirical validation will be put forward. We discuss how these orders impact the complexity of polynomial operations and also the total performance of the encryption scheme as a result. This work will throw light upon optimizing IPCC7 in direction towards efficiency and safety. This research study is expected to further progress post-quantum cryptography because it could specify configurations of the polynomials that will be much more efficient in terms of security and may have better features in terms of performance. Furthermore, compare all available techniques based on how much security they give with post-quantum encryption using parameters such as security, size of key, encryption speed, and computational efficiency.

title: Computational Analysis of DNP3 Security Implementations for Smart Grid
abs: Secure supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) communications in modern smart grid architectures rely on a range of industrial protocols, including DNP3, to support reliable wide area monitoring and control. Utilities face evolving cybersecurity requirements that emphasize confidentiality, integrity, and authentication. Consequently, it is important to assess how these security requirements impact SCADA traffic performance across protocols like Distributed Network Protocol 3 (DNP3), to ensure critical real-time reliability. This paper investigates the operational considerations associated with three practical security approaches for DNP3: baseline operation without security enhancements, protocol-native Secure Authentication Version 6 (SAv6), and DNP3 over Transport Layer Security (TLS). The study uses a testbed that emulates realistic control center to field Wide Area Network (WAN) conditions. The work examines latency behavior, computational demands on resource-constrained devices, and control-plane implications for each security method. The paper defines a structured overhead taxonomy, and identifies relevant performance metrics for supervisory control applications. The paper further presents a decision framework to help utilities select DNP3 security implementations that align with regulatory expectations and operational reliability. It also discusses future transitions toward quantum-resilient cryptographic options for legacy and next generation grid communication assets.

title: Security-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Post-Quantum Cryptography Intelligence
abs: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems have become popular tools for adding external information sources to Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance their capabilities. However, there are significant concerns connected with their use in cybersecurity sectors, such as the possibility of hallucinations, vulnerability to rapid injection attacks, and difficulties in confirming the reliability of the sources that are retrieved. This study proposes a production-grade, security-aware RAG framework designed for cybersecurity knowledge management and Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) intelligence in order to overcome these issues. Multiple security-focused improvements are included in the proposed system, such as evidence-based abstention controlled by a confidence threshold of 0.4, prompt injection defense mechanisms that achieve 100% detection on known attack patterns, multi-source agreement verification that requires corroboration across trusted sources, and trust-weighted retrieval with authority-based scoring-assigning weights of $\mathbf{1. 0}$ to NIST standards and 0.95 to CVE databases. The system generates answers to technical queries with a mean confidence score of 0.719 after processing nine NIST standard publications totaling 2.78 million characters. The addition of security-aware constraints considerably lowers hallucination rates while maintaining query accuracy, according to experimental results. With the addition of cryptographic metadata annotation to FAISS-based vector retrieval, the implementation uses the HuggingFace SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct model for text generation and sentencetransformers to produce 384-dimensional embeddings.

title: Digital Twin and Native-AI Empowered 6G Networks: Architectures, Applications, Evaluation, and Open Challenges
abs: To support these new 6G requirements of high levels of automation, intelligence and reliability, Digital Twins (DTs) will be the base layer to allow for Predictive Assurance, Risk Aware Orchestration, and 'what if' analysis for all layers of the RAN, Edge, and Core. At the same time, as Native Artificial Intelligence (Native-AI), Machine Learning (ML) will be integrated into Control Loops and Data Paths, which will represent an evolution from "AI For Networks" to "AI In Networks," subject to explicit Budget Constraints and Operational Guardrails. The authors make four contributions to this research: (i) A Standards Aligned Reference Architecture, that enables DT Instances to be connected to Native-AI Services through E2/A1/O1 Interfaces; (ii) A Budget Aware Control Framework with Shadow Testing, Canary Deployment, and Automated Rollback; (iii) Case Studies demonstrating SLA Assurance for eMBB/URLLC and Energy Aware Operation using Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS); and (iv) A Security Posture that includes post quantum cryptography, zero trust principles, and complete artefact provenance. The authors show in their extensive emulations a reduction in SLA risk of 30-38%, while keeping control overhead at less than 5%, and 18-24% radio unit energy saving with minimal impact on throughput. They also describe Operator Considerations and highlight Interoperability and Reproducibility Challenges and present a Roadmap towards certified DT + Native-AI operational stacks by 2030-2035.

title: Hardware Design of Optimized Schoolbook-Based Finite Field Multiplications on FPGAs
abs: Finite-field multiplication (FFM) is a fundamental operation in modern cryptographic systems, which underpins core arithmetic computations. However, as operand sizes increase, the associated hardware complexity increases significantly, leading to higher resource consumption and longer processing latency. This paper presents a FFM architecture based on an optimized Schoolbook Multiplication (SBM) algorithm designed to address these challenges. The proposed optimized schoolbook-based finite field multiplication (SBFFM) design is evaluated using the area delay product (ADP) metric to balance hardware resource utilization and computational efficiency. Hardware implementations were performed on a diverse set of FPGA platforms, including Spartan-6 (xc6slx45T-3fgg484), Virtex-5 (xc6slx75), Zynq (xcx7z030), Spartan-7 (xc7s100), Spartan-3E (xc3s100e), Virtex7 (xc7v2000tf), Virtex-4 (vfx60ff1152), Artix-7 (xc7a200t) and Zynq-104 devices. All hardware implementations were performed using the Xilinx ISE platform. Experimental results indicate that the proposed architecture consistently achieves a lower combinational delay compared to existing state-of-the-art multipliers, confirming its effectiveness and practicality for high-performance cryptographic applications.

title: Optimizing Post-Quantum Cryptographic Algorithms for Resource-Constrained Devices
journal: 2026 14th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abs: This paper presents three novel contributions to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) implementation on resource-constrained devices: (1) the first comprehensive benchmarking of NTRU, U-LP, LP, and BLISS schemes across three hardware tiers (desktop, ARMv7 embedded, ATmega2560 microcontroller); (2) optimized implementations incorporating precomputed NTT tables that reduce polynomial multiplication time by 43% on ARMv7 platforms and uniform noise sampling that eliminates decryption failures in U-LP encryption; and (3) practical deployment case studies demonstrating BLISS signatures achieving 1.8s signing on ATmega2560 and U-LP enabling zero-failure LoRaWAN firmware updates. Our results establish that with appropriate optimisations, lattice-based cryptosystems achieve acceptable throughput (0.3-2.1s per operation) on ultra-constrained platforms, though memory-security tradeoffs persist. This work provides concrete implementation guidelines for quantum-resistant cryptography in IoT and embedded systems.

title: Design and Analysis of Energy Efficient ASCON 80Pq
journal: 2026 14th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abs: This paper presents the energy efficient design of ASCON 80pq with performance analysis of cryptographic algorithm for lightweight, post quantum secure applications. ASCON, a lightweight cryptographic scheme, has been recently standardized by national institute of standards and technology (NIST) as part of its Lightweight Cryptography project due to its power efficiency and robust security features. This paper presents the novel secure hardware implementation of ASCON 80pq and compares with its predecessor ASCON 128, balancing power, area, and performance tradeoffs. The implementation of a Verilog RTL analyzes key performance metrics such as throughput, dynamic power consumption, and area efficiency. The power optimization technique, such as clock gating, is demonstrated to significantly reduce dynamic power while preserving performance. The results of FPGA and ASIC implementations prove potential benefits of ASCON 80pq over its predecessor counterpart and make it more efficient cryptographic solutions for IoT systems.

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography for Web Authentication Protocols: A Systematic Review of OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, and SAML Migration
journal: 2026 14th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abs: OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC), and SAML rely on classical public-key primitives such as RSA and ECDSA, which are vulnerable to quantum attacks via Shor's algorithm. This systematic review examines migration of these protocols to Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) following the 2024 NIST standardization of ML-DSA and ML-KEM. We map cryptographic dependencies across all three protocols, evaluate NIST-standardized algorithms for authentication use cases, and analyze practical migration challenges. Token size explosion, with ML-DSA-65 signatures approximately 52 times larger than ECDSA P-256, represents the dominant implementation barrier, compounded by incomplete JOSE standardization and limited ecosystem maturity. Missing formal security proofs and federation migration frameworks are identified as critical priorities before production deployment.

title: Performance Evaluation of Post-Quantum Cryptography in IoT: A Case Study on MQTT Over TLS Under Network Constraints
journal: 2026 14th International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security (ISDFS)
abs: The imminent advent of quantum computing poses a significant threat to current asymmetric cryptographic standards, such as RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC), widely used in Internet of Things (IoT) protocols. This paper evaluates the performance impact of migrating to Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) in an MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) environment secured by TLS. We propose a reproducible benchmark framework based on containerization (Docker) and hardware emulation (QEMU/ARM64) to simulate resource-constrained IoT devices. We compared the handshake latency of standard TLS against a hybrid implementation utilizing NIST-standardized PQC algorithms: ML-KEM-768 (Key Encapsulation) and ML-DSA-65 (Digital Signature). Experiments conducted under controlled network impairments (latency, jitter, and packet loss) revealed that PQC introduces an approximate 4.7x increase in connection establishment time compared to classical TLS, primarily due to computational overhead on the ARM64 architecture. However, message publication latency posthandshake remains negligible. These findings suggest that while PQC is viable for IoT, it necessitates architectural shifts towards persistent sessions to mitigate initial handshake costs.

title: Hybrid QKD-AES Integration: Enhancing BB84-Based Quantum Key Distribution for Practical Encryption
journal: International Conference on AI Engineering and Innovations (AIEI)
abs: The concept of quantum Key Distribution (QKD) has become a critical security tool of the post-quantum world that provides information-theoretic security to cryptographic exchange of keys. In this paper, we build our earlier study on the simulation of the BB84 protocol by incorporating the use of QKD-generated symmetric keys in the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) to encrypt data safely. The hybrid QKD-AES model fills the gap between quantum key generation and classical encryption, guaranteeing quantum-safe key distribution and efficient data confidentiality. We have shown that our implementation is practically feasible with better accuracy and lower key error rates, and enhanced end-to-end encryption reliability as compared to the baseline BB84 simulation. The suggested architecture demonstrates the ease with which QKD keys can be integrated into the existing encryption infrastructure in a harmonious manner, which opens the way to deploying hybrid cryptography infrastructures that are viable to be used in the real world. This is in contrast to protocol-level extensions of BB84 which concentrate on a system level integration framework formalizing the secure transfer of keys between quantum key generation and classical AES encryption without loss of synchronization or integrity of keys. To investigate the performance of QBER sensitivity and key reliability, performance evaluation will involve controlled simulation of various simulated parameters of quantum channels, such as quantum noise, photon loss, etc.

title: A Hybrid PQC-Enabled Attribute and Data Encryption Pipeline for Next-Generation Metaverse Platforms
journal: International Conference on Secure IoT, Assured and Trusted Computing (SATC)
abs: The metaverse requires secure, low-latency, and finegrained access control mechanisms capable of supporting realtime communication and high-volume immersive data. Conventional Ciphertext-Policy Attribute-Based Encryption (CP-ABE) schemes are unsuitable for these environments because their computational overhead grows with the number of attributes and policy complexity, leading to unacceptable latency for resourceconstrained VR/AR devices. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a hybrid post-quantum CP-ABE framework that encrypts only a compact AES session key under attribute-based policies, while large metaverse data objects are protected using AES-GCM. This design ensures that CP-ABE operations remain lightweight and independent of payload size, enabling efficient real-time data sharing. The framework incorporates a dual-plane architecture consisting of a Quantum-Resilient Control Plane which utilizes Kyber Key Encapsulation Mechanisms (KEM) for secure channel establishment and Dilithium signatures for identity assurance and a Low-Latency Data Plane, where avatars execute only symmetric-key operations. Heavy CP-ABE decryption tasks are delegated to a dedicated Decryptor Peer (DP), substantially reducing client-side computation and improving scalability across diverse metaverse scenarios. An evaluation of the proposed approach demonstrates that CP-ABE latency remains nearly constant across attribute sets ranging from 2 to 2000, while AES-GCM maintains stable performance regardless of policy size. Overall, the proposed framework offers quantum-resilient security, fine-grained attribute enforcement, and low-latency performance, establishing a practical and scalable solution for secure real-time metaverse communication.

title: Securing IoT Devices in the Quantum Era: AI-Based Detection with Hybrid Post-Quantum Encryption
journal: International Conference on Secure IoT, Assured and Trusted Computing (SATC)
abs: With the advancement of quantum computing, the long-term security of IoT systems is increasingly challenged, particularly due to the vulnerability of traditional public-key cryptography. This study integrates artificial intelligence (AI) with a hybrid strategy that involves Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) and Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) to address this challenge. Incoming traffic from the TON-IoT dataset is processed by AI using XGBoost, Random Forest, and One-Class SVM as anomaly-detection filters. Only traffic classified as normal is forwarded to the encryption phase. Postquantum key establishment is performed using Kyber-512, and the resulting shared secret is combined with simulated BB84based QKD key material via a key-derivation function (KDF) to derive a 256-bit session key, which is then used with AES-256GCM for authenticated IoT data encryption. Experimental results demonstrate that the hybrid algorithm, along with the AI, can effectively improve IoT security. Upon optimization of the parameter $\beta(=1.0)$, the Delivery Purity is 0.92, the Data Delivery rate is 0.80, and the Secure Delivery $\mathrm{F} \beta$ score is 0.94 compared to Delivery Purity of 0.77, Delivery Rate of 1.0, and Secure Delivery Fβ score of 0.87, respectively, without AI.

title: SAPH-Kyber: Stage-Aware Pipeline Hardening for CRYSTALS-Kyber NTT Against Transient Faults
journal: International Conference on Secure IoT, Assured and Trusted Computing (SATC)
abs: As lattice-based cryptography transitions into global standards, the physical security of hardware implementations like CRYSTALS-Kyber against side-channel vulnerabilities has become a critical research priority. This paper presents a comprehensive temporal sensitivity analysis of a Kyber Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) hardware core under transient fault conditions. Utilizing a custom-built Verilog simulation framework, we perform an automated sensitivity sweep by injecting single-cycle glitches into the arithmetic pipeline across all seven NTT stages. Our results reveal a significant Error Diffusion Gradient: faults in the initial pipeline stages ($0-2$) result in global polynomial corruption, affecting all 256 coefficients, whereas latestage faults remain localized to as few as two coefficients. We characterize the predictable mathematical leakage resulting from these faults (e.g., error magnitudes of 34 and 67) and demonstrate their exploitability for secret key recovery via Differential Fault Analysis (DFA). Based on these findings, we propose a Selective Pipeline Hardening strategy that concentrates hardware protection such as parity-based error detection on high-diffusion temporal windows (Stages 0-3). This targeted approach provides robust security with a significant reduction in area and power overhead compared to traditional full-core redundancy, offering a scalable methodology for securing post-quantum processors in resource-constrained FPGA and ASIC environments.

title: Adaptive-AI-Zerotrust-Chain: AI-Centric Zero Trust Enforcement for IoT Security
journal: International Conference on Secure IoT, Assured and Trusted Computing (SATC)
abs: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has intensified demand for robust, adaptive security frameworks. This paper introduces Adaptive-AI-ZeroTrustChain (AAZTC), an adaptive mechanism integrating AI-driven dynamic trust boundary modeling with blockchain-based verifiable access logging for granular, auditable zero-trust enforcement. The architecture employs deep reinforcement learning for continuous behavioral analysis and trust score computation, while leveraging smart contracts on a permissioned blockchain for immutable access decision records. A lightweight post-quantum cryptographic module ensures future-proof security. Experiments on CICIDS2017 dataset demonstrate that AAZTC achieves 99.12 % detection accuracy, 98.45 % precision, and 98.87 % F1-score, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by $\mathbf{3. 2 - 5. 8 \%}$. NSL-KDD is included only as a legacy baseline. The system maintains average trust decision times of $\mathbf{1 2. 4}$ milliseconds, suitable for real-time IoT deployments.

title: PQ-MQTT: A Hybrid Post-Quantum Secure Communication Protocol for MQTT-Based IoT Networks
journal: International Conference on Secure IoT, Assured and Trusted Computing (SATC)
abs: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices that use the Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol poses significant security challenges in the emerging quantum computing era. Current Transport Layer Security (TLS) implementations rely on classical cryptographic algorithms vulnerable to Shor's algorithm. This paper proposes PQ-MQTT, a hybrid post-quantum secure communication protocol that integrates ML-KEM-768 with X25519 for key encapsulation and a lightweight session-key derivation mechanism optimized for resource-constrained IoT publishers. We present a formal security analysis under the Quantum Random Oracle Model (QROM), demonstrating resilience against store-now-decryptlater attacks. Experimental evaluation on the Raspberry Pi 4, ESP32, and Arduino Nano 33 platforms shows that PQ-MQTT achieves handshake latencies of $127.3 ~\text{ms}, 412.7 ~\text{ms}$, and $1,847.2 ~\text{ms}$, respectively, with 18.2 KB of additional memory overhead. A comparative analysis of pure post-quantum and classical TLS implementations shows energy reductions of $23.5 \%-40.5 \%$ relative to pure PQC, achieved through our hybrid optimization approach, while maintaining 94.2 % throughput efficiency.

title: Post-Quantum Authentication for Resource-Constrained IoT: A Comparative Study of Hash-Based Signatures on RP2350
journal: International Conference on Secure IoT, Assured and Trusted Computing (SATC)
abs: The emergence of quantum computing threatens classical cryptographic systems protecting IoT infrastructure. This study addresses the challenge of implementing postquantum authentication on resource-constrained devices by evaluating hash-based signature schemes on the RP2350 microcontroller. Three authentication approaches are implemented and benchmarked: HMAC-SHA256 (classical baseline), Lamport one-time signatures, and Winternitz onetime signatures with Merkle trees. All implementations integrate Physical Unclonable Functions (PUF) for hardwarerooted key derivation, eliminating persistent key storage vulnerabilities. Experimental evaluation across three Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W devices measures key generation time, signing latency, verification overhead, memory consumption, and transmission size under realistic temperature sensor workloads. Results demonstrate that Winternitz signatures achieve post-quantum security with 2.1KB signatures and 55-183ms signing time, representing 74% size reduction and $3 \times$ performance improvement over Lamport while maintaining equivalent security. A hybrid authentication model is proposed, combining Winternitz signatures for periodic device authentication with HMAC for continuous sensor data transmission, balancing post-quantum security with operational efficiency. This work provides the first comprehensive performance characterisation of hash-based signatures on RP2350, offering practical guidance for IoT developers transitioning to post-quantum cryptography in resource-constrained environments.

title: A Web-Based Quantum Key Distribution Simulator with Adaptive Post-Quantum Cryptography Fallback
journal: International Conference on Expert Clouds and Applications (ICOECA)
abs: The rapid advancement of quantum computing poses a critical threat to conventional cryptographic systems such as RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC). To address this challenge, two major paradigms have emerged: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), which leverages quantum mechanics for theoretically unbreakable key exchange, and Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), which relies on mathematically hard problems resilient to quantum attacks. Current research demonstrates the potential of integrating. QKD with lattice-based PQC to achieve hybrid quantum resilience; however, most existing works remain theoretical or infrastructure-centric, lacking accessible and interactive implementations. This paper presents the design and implementation of a web-based QKD simulation platform featuring a real-time security scorecard and an automatic PQC fallback mechanism using CRYSTALS-Kyber. Built on the BB84 protocol, the simulator models quantum communication between Alice, Bob, and Eve under various channel conditions and computes key performance metrics such as Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER), Secret Key Rate (SKR), and efficiency, and dynamically switches to Kyber when QKD reliability degrades. Unlike prior studies, the proposed system emphasizes interactivity, visualization, and hybrid resilience, providing a practical tool for education, research, and industry experimentation. The resulting platform bridges the gap between theoretical hybrid cryptography and real-world deployment, advancing the broader adoption of quantum-safe communication systems.

title: Quantum Cryptography: Feasibility Of Post-Quantum Algorithms for Secure Communication
journal: International Conference on Expert Clouds and Applications (ICOECA)
abs: The security underpinnings of extensively used encrypted public-key systems are in danger due to the development of massive-scale quantum computation. Digital interactions are now protected by methods like RSA and the Elliptic Curve encryption, which depend on computational challenges that can be effectively resolved by quantum computations. The use of (PQC) studies, which attempts to create secure systems immune from both traditional and quantum threats, has intensified as a result of this growing worry. Specified traditional techniques (such as RSA- 2048 and ECC- P256), and exemplary futuristic systems (Kyber, Dilithium, SPHINCS +, and Classic McEliece) are systematically evaluated for viability in this paper. A single application architecture is used for deploying every algorithm and useful metrics for performance like time taken to execute, key terms of size, and encrypted content or the signature size are used to evaluate them. The contrast study shows that lattice-driven new quantum algorithms offer a better fair tradeoff between integrity and effectiveness, while also highlighting the overpowering computational cost of conventional approaches. The findings provide useful information about the post- quantum cryptography solutions' preparedness for next reliable interaction systems.

title: Enhanced QR-MCP Framework: A Quantum-Resistant Multipath Cryptographic Protocol with AI-Driven Anomaly Detection
journal: International Conference on Next-Gen Quantum and Advanced Computing: Algorithms, Security, and Beyond (NQComp)
abs: Cryptographic protocols that combine quantum resistance, operational efficiency, and autonomous defense are necessary for the shift to post-quantum security. This paper presents the Enhanced QR-MCP Framework, a self-healing crypto-network that uses multipath communication, SPHINCS+ signatures, and Lattice-Based Cryptography (LBC). The framework includes two key innovations: (1) Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) capability, which allows process-without-decrypting functionality for perpetual confidentiality at intermediate nodes; and (2) Adaptive AI-Based Route Reconfiguration using ensemble learning (Isolation Forest, Random Forest, SVM, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) for real-time anomaly detection and network self-healing. Enhanced QR-MCP uses algorithmic optimization to achieve better performance: Adaptive Segment Size and Parallel Asynchronous PQC Key Establishment separates lattice operations from data transmission. In contrast to 40.97 ms for Tor, the encryption latency for 4096-byte messages is 61.44 ms, with a decryption latency of 57.34 ms. FHE (204.8 ms) and ZKP verification (122.88 ms) are optional security layers. Simulation testing showed that anomaly detection detected illegal traffic and unauthorized access in real time, reducing network-based attacks by more than 70%. Through multipath fragmentation and SPHINCS+ signature verification, the protocol thwarts side-channel, traffic analysis, Man-in-the-Middle, and collusion attacks. In order to secure 5G/6G and cloud environments, enhanced QR-MCP provides a workable, deployable solution that combines autonomous threat response with quantum resistance through SVP/LWE-based cryptography.

title: Quantum Communication Redefined: Three-Layer Quantum Communication Protocol for Secure and Covert Transmission
journal: International Conference on Next-Gen Quantum and Advanced Computing: Algorithms, Security, and Beyond (NQComp)
abs: Classical cryptography methods are becoming susceptible to quantum attacks like those implemented by Shor and Grover algorithms and can break RSA and symmetric-key encryption. Traditional communication channels are also susceptible to interception and even modification of the signal that causes data confidentiality to be compromised. In order to overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a three-layer quantum-hybrid communication framework, which integrates entanglement-based QKD, multi-channel redundancy, and steganographic hiding. The framework improves the security with an entanglement-assisted BB84-based protocol, the reliability with the help of multi-channel qubit transmission, and covert transmission with LSB/DCT-image embedding. The framework is developed and implemented as a simulator in Python using Qiskit, NumPy, and OpenCV and showed better Bit Error Rate (BER), SSIM, fidelity and security strength than classical systems. The proposed architecture mitigates key vulnerabilities in cryptographic strength, transmission stability, and communication detectability, providing a robust foundation for quantum-resilient and covert communication.

title: Software Defined Networking (SDN)-Enabled Machine Learning Approach for Resource Allocation in Quantum Key Distribution Networks
journal: International Conference on Next-Gen Quantum and Advanced Computing: Algorithms, Security, and Beyond (NQComp)
abs: Quantum cryptography is one of the emerging nascent fields in the area of quantum computing. It has found its places in various diversified applications across the domains. Ensuring long term information security in the post-quantum era requires the redesigning of conventional algorithms, which are quantum resistant. In the post quantum era, the field of quantum cryptography promises trusted communications, but practical implementation of the networks suffers serious challenges from adaptive conditions like noise and failures of the network links. Revaluation of new quantum resistant security algorithms need to be considered. This paper presents a hybrid system that combines Machine Learning (ML), Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) along with software-defined networking (SDN) for real-time allocation of resources in quantum networks. This approach uses the random forest classifier to predict a different robust network path based on the key rate and quantum bit error rate parameters. As network conditions change, the SDN controller makes it possible to choose a dynamic link. The simulations methods show that the system can adapt to increased noise and compromised links and attain key rates of up to 12.5 Mbps with a QBER rate as low as 0.01. In comparison to manual resource allocation in quantum networks, simulation findings demonstrate greater adaptability and security. Software-defined networking (SDN), quantum bit error rate (QBER), quantum key distribution (QKD), post-quantum cryptography (PQC), machine learning, and resource allocation are the index terms. Results show higher adaptability and security with respect to manual allocation of resources in quantum networks.

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Linux Distribution
journal: International Conference on Next-Gen Quantum and Advanced Computing: Algorithms, Security, and Beyond (NQComp)
abs: In this research work, the classic cryptography methods on which modern digital security relies are threatened by an existential risk due to the development of quantum computing. When large-scale quantum computing emerges, algorithms such as RSA, ECC, & Diffie-Hellman, having protected data for several decades, might soon turn vulnerable. This has created a direct need across the globe to migrate to post-quantum cryptographic techniques that can also resist attacks by adversaries, both classical and quantum. In this paper, we authors use the Yocto Project to develop and deploy a PQC-enabled Linux distribution. The system presents a hybrid encryption architecture for quantum-safe file security, combining symmetric encryption using AES-256 with simulated key encapsulation based on CRYSTALS-Kyber. The creation of a special meta-layer known as meta-pqr allows Yocto to be expanded with PQC-specific recipes, system services, and cryptographic tools. A completely automated file encryption daemon transparently encrypts newly created files in real-time while monitoring filesystem events without requiring user input. Platform independence and reproducibility are assured since the entire system is designed, packaged, and tested in a controlled embedded environment built around a QEMU. With thorough functional verification, runtime evaluation, and security assessment, the proposed PQC Linux distribution exhibits reliability, low-latency encryption, stable resource consumption, and seamless integration with embedded Linux workflows. This work provides a validated, modular, and extensible operating system blueprint for PQC-enabled systems that can be used as a foundation for additional research and deployment in quantum-resilient infrastructures.

title: Development of Quantum-Ready Digital Wallet using Blockchain by Integrating Post- Quantum Cryptography, Dynamic Fees, and Proof-of-Work Consensus
journal: International Conference on Next-Gen Quantum and Advanced Computing: Algorithms, Security, and Beyond (NQComp)
abs: The integration of blockchain technology with almost all sectors can bring positive transformation and a future influence on digital transactions. So far as the development of quantum computers has been achieved, it's necessary for blockchain security to explore quantum-resistant cryptographic techniques. This study inspects the production of a blockchain system with an adjustable transaction payment model, and introduces quantum resistant cryptography. Basically, the system attempts to compensate for the inherent security flaws in each of the conventional blockchains by authenticating and verifying transactions using Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC)-based signatures, using conventional quantum-safe digital wallets. The project also looks at a dynamic fee setting to optimize transaction processing during periods of network congestion and a Proof-of-Work (PoW) consensus mechanism to lock the blockchain further. Finally, This paper would simulate the E91 quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol so as to examine the security features that are provided by the entanglement effects. Unlike the more commonly employed BB84 scoring system, the E91 scheme involves the discovery of eavesdropping through the breach of Bell inequality, and thus provides a unique approach to modular authentication of key swap in decentralized environment.

title: Architecting a Quantum-Safe Transport Layer: An Integrated QKD-PQC Protocol for Point-to-Point Security
journal: International Conference on Next-Gen Quantum and Advanced Computing: Algorithms, Security, and Beyond (NQComp)
abs: The exponential development of quantum computing represents a serious threat to the existence of the modern cybersecurity infrastructure. Fault-tolerant large-scale quantum computing will be realized roughly five to ten years hence, and will make most of the current standards for asymmetric cryptography-such as RSA and ECC-deviant. While mitigations, such as Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) and Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) offer possible countermeasures, both are hampered by vulnerabilities of their own. Respectively, PQC relies on unproven mathematical hardness assumptions that are always subject to future algorithmic innovations, while QKD is limited by the physical requirements of a dedicated quantum channel. This paper presents a new hybrid protocol which aims to solve these limitations by combining PQC and QKD into a unified design. The proposed scheme will hybridize the secure key resulting from the BB84-based QKD protocol with a second secret derived by using a lattice-based PQC key exchange, using a strong hybrid key derivation function. It deals with a point-to-point transport-layer model, which is in line with the technological limitations of QKD models at present. The implementation would need trusted nodes or quantum repeaters, which are beyond the reach of this implementation. The system is implemented on a dual-channel platform: the quantum channel is used for key distribution and the classical channel is used for PQC negotiation and secure data transmission, all classical communication is authenticated by HMAC. The resulting architecture is a future-proof quantum-safe communication system that will protect government sensitive data, as well as financial and e-commerce enterprises, thus ensuring the transition to a quantum resistant digital society in the face of a catastrophic event that would have a massive financial and societal impact.

title: A Cross-Layer Survey on Lattice-Based Post-Quantum Cryptography: Side-Channel Security, Hardware Design, and Secure IoT Protocol Integration
journal: International Conference on Next-Gen Quantum and Advanced Computing: Algorithms, Security, and Beyond (NQComp)
abs: Lattice-based cryptography has emerged as the leading candidate for post-quantum public-key primitives due to strong worst-case hardness guarantees and efficient algebraic structure. As standardization efforts mature, practical deployment increasingly depends on implementation security, hardware feasibility, and protocol-level robustness rather than theoretical security alone. This survey presents a cross-layer analysis integrating recent experimental and analytical results across these dimensions. At the implementation level, we review non-profiled correlation power and electromagnetic attacks targeting polynomial multiplication and NTT-based arithmetic. At the hardware layer, we analyze building-block cost models and ASIC/FPGA trade-offs for NTT, Toom─Cook, and schoolbook multipliers, highlighting performance, memory, and leakage implications. At the protocol layer, we examine reconciliation-enabled RLWE authenticated key exchange schemes for constrained IoT devices and their associated attack surfaces. By consolidating attack vectors, implementation trade-offs, and cross-layer interactions, this survey provides practical guidance for designing secure, efficient, and deployable lattice-based post-quantum systems.

title: HQRMLE: A Quantum-Resistant Blockchain Framework for Secure and Privacy-Preserving Healthcare Data Management
journal: International Conference on Next-Gen Quantum and Advanced Computing: Algorithms, Security, and Beyond (NQComp)
abs: Widespread EHR adoption proved to be a great strategic win in terms of data access and clinical interoperability but also raised too many serious concerns involving confidentiality, integrity, and regulatory compliance. The major security solutions for healthcare today are based on only classical cryptographic primitives and blockchain-based access control, but dealing with their limitations once faced with not-so-far-fetched quantum threats and the requirements introduced by privacy-preserving analytics. This paper proposes a Hybrid Quantum-Resistant Multi-Layer Encryption, a layered scheme that couples post-quantum cryptography with attribute-based encryption, fully homomorphic encryption, DID/ZKP and smart contracts based on the blockchain. Instead of serving just one approach to blockchain or PQC, HQRMLE will provide quantum-resistant master-key construction, fine-grained access control, encrypted calculation, and an immutable audit framework all knitted into one unified architecture. Specific security and privacy metrics have been established defining the performance of the system. Experimental evaluation with real-world health care datasets demonstrates that HQRMLE outperforms traditional, quantum, and insider threats with new interpretation integration. This approach comes with an immanent low-cost on-chain storage overhead and a more acceptable computational overhead intrinsic to a pragmatic balance between efficiency and security. The results indicate that HQRMLE is a deployable and compliant framework that embraces next-generation data management for healthcare.
